blind.why: Mid-range haze in a corridor (m_haze_3, Long Ramp, pop at 38,1.57,-15, seen from 12 m) vs CS2 t4_024. CS2's smoke hugs the ground, spreads with wispy, uneven edges and takes on the scene's colour. Ours is a bright white cumulus 'cotton ball' with a flat bottom edge that sits in the corridor like a pasted-in sprite. Up close you can see round puff outlines like bubble-wrap (zpunch.png).

Shooting through smoke (m_punch0, 6 pistol shots) vs CS2 t4_023. In CS2 the tracer tears an irregular channel and the smoke thins along it. Ours makes a tiny round peephole about crosshair-sized (~14 px at 640 wide, ~1 deg) with a hard bright rim, like a decal. From 0.5 s it reads as a faint glow (m_punch05).

Smoke against walls and props, side view (m_side) vs CS2 t4_015. CS2's smoke spills around the dumpster with soft, dissolving fringes. Ours is a dense lobed white mass with a crisp silhouette. It fills the alley convincingly but looks like clay rather than vapour.

biggest_gap: Bot Strobes blind their own team far more often than the enemy. I ran 2 rich bot-lab matches (test=1&scene=bot-lab&view=none, seeds 2 and 5, credits 9000, 4 rounds each) and logged util:blind. There were 11 bot strobes. Only 3 blinded an enemy at amount >=0.5. 10 blinded the thrower or a teammate at amount >=0.5. Examples: seed 2 R3, Sable's strobe at Upper Tunnel blinded You 0.91 and Blitz 0.91 and no enemies. Seed 5 R1, Marlo's strobe on Long Ramp hit 3 teammates and 0 enemies. Seed 5 R2, Quill popped a strobe 0.4 m from You (0.56). The human player was team-flashed 4 times in 8 rounds. In CS2 bots pop flashes past a corner or over a wall into the enemy area, after turning away or with teammates looking away. Fix (src/ai/bots/throws.js lineups + release check): before release, simulate u.trajectory, then run strobe.evaluate for every teammate and the thrower at the predicted pop point. Abort or re-aim when any ally would get >0.3. Pick pop points on the enemy side of a wall or corner from the region graph, and have the thrower turn away during the fuse.
other_gaps: Haze look is still a cumulus of identical round impostor puffs. Disc outlines are visible at 12 m (zpunch.png), the bottom edge is flat and hard, and there are no ground-hugging wisps or drifting fringe. It looks the same from 1 s to 13 s. CS2 (t4_015/t4_024) has ragged, wispy edges, ground spread and visible churn. Needed: per-puff noise erosion strong enough to hide the sprite discs, a low skirt that spreads along the floor, and slow advection or billowing.

The punch-through tunnel is too small and too clean. After 6 shots at 12 m both the visible hole and the LOS-clear cone are only about 1 deg wide (opticalDepth is 0 at 4 px off-axis and 4.3 at 8 px, at 640x360). On screen it is a crisp round hole with a bright rim (m_punch0). Render and LOS now agree, which is the fix from r1. But a spray should open a ragged channel big enough to see a head, with a soft, noisy edge and no white halo.

Strobe at amount 0.98 is not full white. The left and right thirds of the screen stay mid-grey because of a heavy vignette (s_1.6, s_2.5), so the centre reads as a bright vertical band. CS2's full flash is uniform white edge to edge, and the burnt-in afterimage is clearly visible. No afterimage was visible here under SwiftShader.

Bots throw little utility. With 9000 credits each, 10 bots made 7 throws in 4 rounds (seed 2) and 15 in 4 rounds (seed 5). Only 1 haze landed in seed 2, late on Terrace. Seed 5 attackers smoked their own approach twice in one round, two hazes on Long Ramp at their own feet (38.1,-7.4 and 36.6,-6) instead of the defender cross or CT angle.

The long throw has no feedback at range. My strong haze from Long Ramp flew 28 m and popped behind the A crates, and it shows as a postage-stamp white patch (r_haze_*). The aim preview in the map is still a short cyan vertical streak (r_aim) rather than a readable arc with a landing ring.
Pulse is now distinct (hex dome, dust, sparks, no whiteout), but the dust ball at 0.6 s (p_2.1) is a flat beige billboard wall filling the corridor, with soft cut edges at the walls.
bugs: Bot strobe lineups routinely flash the thrower and teammates (see biggest_gap). 2 of 11 strobes self-blinded the thrower at >=0.49 (Zed 0.85, Cobalt 0.57).
Seed 5 R2: two bots threw hazes onto the same spot on Long Ramp within seconds, which wastes utility (no claim/dedupe on smoke targets).
strengths: Render and LOS now agree on punch-through. The hole's on-screen radius (~7 px) matches where blocksLine flips from clear to blocked (4-8 px), and the wake refills on screen and in LOS together (0 at 0.5 s, 0.3 at 1.2 s, 4.7 at 1.8 s, 6.7 at 2.5 s).
Corridor fill is now confined and long: 3200 cells, 17.5 m span, 0 leak. It blocks lines across the whole corridor width (fan of 17 lines all blocked, od 4.9-9.2).
Throw physics remain deterministic and robust: stairs, wall rebounds, run and jump-throw inheritance. The kill plane now despawns out-of-world grenades.
Pulse has its own identity: blue/magenta hex dome, ring, dust, confetti. It deals sensible falloff damage (5 at 6 m, 49 near), and walls block it.
The builder suite now completes 31/31 with no console errors. The real map and both matches were error-free, and smoke adds no measurable render cost.
